audit.whatIsWrong: The page called this FAVOURED at 4/10 and 'one of LeBlanc's most favorable across the entire game' while she wins 50.53% of 1589 games.
audit.why: A coin-flip win rate cannot be one of the champion's best matchups. The rating and the sentence that repeats it both had to move.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN, diffRating 5.5/10, tone amber, breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t restated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game spike text said Ziggs has 'no innate escape besides his ultimate's minor knockback utility'.
audit.why: The knockback is Satchel Charge (W), not Mega Inferno Bomb — Riot's W text says the explosion knocks enemies away and 'Ziggs is also knocked away, but takes no damage'. That self-knock is his entire escape, and it goes from 20s at rank 1 to 12s at rank 5, so the window you can catch him in shrinks by 8 seconds over the lane. The R is a 5000-range 120/95/70s bomb with no escape component at all.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge's real cooldowns and self-knockback written into breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.carry, spikes[3], early and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers contradicted each other about whether Ziggs has an escape, and the Short Fuse tell was missing.
audit.why: The full layer correctly calls Satchel Charge 'his knockback escape'; the content layer says four separate times that he has 'zero escape' and 'no way to punish her'. One of those is on the page under the other. Separately, Short Fuse periodically arms an empowered auto whose cooldown drops every time he casts an ability — the wind-up, not the bomb, is the tell that damage is coming.
audit.corrected: Content layer aligned to the full layer on the escape; Short Fuse added to dontsFull[0] and the early paragraph.

audit.why: The whole plan is 'catch him while the satchel is down' and the page never said how long that is.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Satchel 20s/12s, Minefield flat 16s, Mega Inferno Bomb 120s at 5000 range.

edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Ziggs carry threat 5/10.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Distortion (return) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge (W): 20s at rank 1, 12s at rank 5 — it knocks him away as well as you, so he is catchable only while it is down. - Hexplosive Minefield (E) is a flat 16s slow zone. - Mega Inferno Bomb reaches 5000 on 120s.

edits.before: Q the sigil, W the detonation, return before the answer — a half-bar round trip he experienced as weather.
edits.after: At 6, Mimic a second Ethereal Chains — two roots inside one Satchel cooldown and he never gets the knockback off.

edits.before: Ziggs burns Satchel Charge on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Ziggs satchels a turret or a wave — that is 20 seconds with no escape.

edits.before: That’s Ziggs’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Short Fuse arms an empowered auto every few seconds — the wind-up is the tell.

edits.before: Staying at the W landing spot for one more auto — the return timer is your champion; outliving it is optional.
edits.after: Coast and his Mega Inferno Bomb reaches 5000 range on a 70-second cooldown — he farms the map you gave him.

edits.before: Ziggs wins by landing Satchel Charge, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Ziggs wins by satchelling out of your commit, laying minefields across your entry, and chipping from 850 range.

edits.before: Carry through picks — one chained carry per objective; your job is the flank angle and the discipline to leave after.
edits.after: Carry through picks — chain him while Satchel Charge is down; 20 seconds at rank 1 is the window, and he owns no second exit.

edits.before: If Ziggs opens the score, reset expectations and respect Satchel Charge doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with W clears and stay relevant through chain picks.
edits.after: If Ziggs opens the score, stop walking through his 900-range minefield and farm from behind the wave. After a second kill: W-clear, wait for the 20-second satchel to be spent, and take picks off-lane.

edits.before: LeBlanc's mobility lets her dodge Ziggs's poke and punish him hard at levels 1-2 since he has zero escape.
edits.after: Your mobility dodges Ziggs's poke and punishes him at levels 1-2, before Satchel Charge is ranked and the escape exists.

edits.before: Ziggs's complete lack of mobility means LeBlanc can still close the distance and burst him down even at a full build.
edits.after: Ziggs owns one escape on a 12-second Satchel Charge, so full-build burst still kills him the moment it has been spent.

edits.before: Even with a completed build, Ziggs remains immobile and relies entirely on never letting LeBlanc close the distance, which her W blink is built to bypass.
edits.after: Even at full build his only exit is a 12-second Satchel Charge that knocks him away — bait it out, then Distortion in while it is down and he has nothing left.

edits.before: LeBlanc completely dominates this matchup from the very first level because Ziggs has no dash, no escape, and no way to punish her once she closes the distance with W. LeBlanc should simply dodge his Bouncing Bomb poke using her mobility and dive in for a kill whenever he's out of position. Ziggs is forced to play at absolute maximum range and pray his minefield deters an all-in.
edits.after: You dominate the early levels because Ziggs has no dash and his only escape, Satchel Charge, is 20 seconds at rank 1. Dodge the Bouncing Bomb poke with your mobility and dive whenever he is out of position. Short Fuse arms an empowered auto every few seconds, so his wind-up is your cue to step out, not the bomb cast. He plays at maximum range and hopes Hexplosive Minefield deters the all-in.

edits.before: This dominance continues uninterrupted into level 6 and beyond, since LeBlanc's Mimic-doubled Ethereal Chains gives her a guaranteed way to root Ziggs in place and finish the combo before he can react in any way. LeBlanc should look to snowball hard and roam off the pressure this lane generates, since Ziggs offers almost nothing in return. Ziggs's only real hope is heavy peel from allies or turret proximity.
edits.after: The pressure continues into level 6 and beyond, since Mimic-doubled Ethereal Chains gives you two roots inside a single Satchel Charge cooldown and he cannot knock himself away from both. Snowball hard and roam off the pressure this lane generates, since Ziggs offers little in return. His real hope is peel from allies, turret proximity, and a satchel he saved rather than spent on the wave.

edits.before: Even at a full build, Ziggs remains completely immobile with no innate escape besides his ultimate's minor knockback utility, meaning LeBlanc's gap-closing W blink continues to make him one of the easiest targets in the game to pick off in skirmishes. His poke damage is real from a distance, but any time LeBlanc can reach him one-on-one the fight is essentially over instantly. This matchup remains one of LeBlanc's most favorable across the entire game.
edits.after: Even at a full build Ziggs is immobile apart from Satchel Charge, a 12-second self-knockback that is his entire escape, so your Distortion entry keeps him one of the easiest targets in the game to pick off in skirmishes. His 850-range poke and a 5000-range Mega Inferno Bomb are real from a distance, but once you reach him one-on-one with the satchel spent the fight is over. Chain first, then burst.
Save Satchel Charge as his escape
